author: template-projects
name: Aspire starter: solution, API and data store
description: The root of a scaffold: an Aspire AppHost, an ASP.NET Core API with EF Core persistence against the data store you choose, shared service defaults and the API test suite. Runnable on its own; add a front end with aspire-ui-react or aspire-ui-blazor and event sourcing with aspire-events.

resource.description: The singular PascalCase name of the sample resource, e.g. Product. The scaffold's entity, controller, page and tests are named from it. The plural is this plus "s" - an irregular plural is a rename after scaffolding, not a second parameter. Pass the SAME value to every template in a scaffold, exactly like -n.

resourceLower.//: The lowercase form, for TypeScript identifiers, route paths and file names. A separate symbol because `replaces` is a literal substitution - unlike sourceName, it does not match case variants.

dbProvider.description: Which store the API reads its data from. Only the provider you pick is scaffolded: the others' migrations projects, packages and code branches are removed rather than shipped unused.

choices.description: PostgreSQL in a container, wired through the Aspire Npgsql integration. Needs Docker.
SQL Server 2022 Express in a container, wired through the Aspire SQL Server integration. Needs Docker.
A local file. No container and no Docker, so `aspire run` comes up anywhere - at the cost of the EF health check the container integrations register.

dbProviderModule.//: IaC/database.tf calls one module, and this is the single line that differs between the three providers. The module directories that were not chosen are excluded below, so a scaffold carries only the one it uses - exactly as it carries only one migrations project.

dbProviderManifest.//: The data store as .aspirestarter.json records it, for the aspire-addon CLI. stage.ps1 writes that file.

nameManifest.//: The -n value verbatim, for .aspirestarter.json. sourceName rewrites contents with the casing of the token it matched, so the lowercase sourceName loses the original casing - which the Blazor add-on, PascalCase throughout, needs back.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic `dotnet restore` after scaffolding.

nameBlazorProject.//: This template's sourceName is the lowercase `template` and the engine matches it case-sensitively, so the PascalCase `Template.Blazor.*` project names that appear in this template's comments and docs are not substituted by it - they would reach a scaffold naming a project that does not exist. The Blazor add-on builds those names from its own sourceName, `Template`, so this keeps the base's references to them in step. Two details are load-bearing: the match is scoped to `Template.Blazor` rather than the bare word, because `Template` alone would also rewrite unrelated PascalCase uses; and the value has to carry the `.Blazor` suffix, because `replaces` swaps the whole matched string for it - a bare name would collapse `Template.Blazor.Maui.Pages` to `<Name>.Maui.Pages`.

modifiers.//: azurerm_container_app declares a block whose name is exactly this template's sourceName, so substitution would rename it and the configuration would stop parsing. The file needs no substitution of its own - every name in it comes from a Terraform local - so copying it byte for byte costs nothing. stage.ps1 enforces that no other .tf file contains the token.
